**Corollary 1.** — Let K be a commutative field, A be a commutative K-algebra generated by finitely many elements, and $\mathfrak{m}$ be a maximal ideal of A.

a) The degree of $A/\mathfrak{m}$ over K is finite.

b) Let Ω be an algebraically closed extension of K. There exists a K-algebra homomorphism from A to Ω with kernel $\mathfrak{m}$.

The K-algebra $A/\mathfrak{m}$ is generated by finitely many elements, and $A/\mathfrak{m}$ is a field. By Theorem 1, the degree of $A/\mathfrak{m}$ is finite; assertion a) follows. Every extension of K of finite degree is isomorphic to a subextension of Ω (V, §4, No. 1, p. 20, Theorem 1); this gives b).

**Corollary 2.** — Let K be a commutative field, $n$ be a natural number, $(P_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of elements of $K[X_1, . . . ,X_n]$, and Ω be an algebraically closed extension of K. The following conditions are equivalent:

(i) The polynomials $P_i$ do not have a common zero in $\Omega^n$.

(ii) There exists a family $(Q_i)_{i\in I}$, with finite support, of elements of $K[X_1, . . . ,X_n]$ such that $\sum_{i\in I}P_iQ_i= 1$.

Denote by A the ring $K[X_1, . . . ,X_n]$ and by $\mathfrak{a}$ the ideal generated by the polynomial $P_i$. Condition (i) means that there are no K-algebra homomorphisms from $A/\mathfrak{a}$ to Ω. If it is satisfied, then by Corollary 1, the ring $A/\mathfrak{a}$ has no maximal ideals and is therefore zero, and 1 belongs to $\mathfrak{a}$. This proves that (i) implies (ii). The implication (ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i) is clear.
